title: AD-WM: Action-Discriminative World Models for Counterfactual Model Predictive Control
why_read: A solid robotics/planning paper addressing a real weakness in world models used for control, with strong reported gains on manipulation benchmarks.
analysis: The paper identifies a subtle but important problem: world models trained to predict what actually happens next are not necessarily good at telling apart different hypothetical actions, which is exactly what planning algorithms need. Their proposed method, AD-WM, adds training objectives that force the model to preserve information distinguishing one action from another, without changing anything at test time. The reported jump from 3.7% to 52% success on a hard manipulation benchmark, and real robot improvements from 42% to 71%, are large enough to suggest a genuine and not just incremental improvement. This is a solid contribution for people working on model-based robot control and planning.
